head.1: omega · AI maintenance for macOS, Linux and Windows
head.2: omega updates and cleans your Mac, Linux or Windows machine like topgrade and Mole, then reads every failure, finds the cause and fixes the config. It works with Homebrew, apt, dnf, pacman, zypper, Flatpak, snap, winget, Scoop and Chocolatey. Picks the best value model from live prices, or runs fully local. Free and open source.

features.2: What changes when an agent runs your maintenance
features.3: Failures get fixed, not just reported

features.9: The best value model, checked daily

features.13: Your toolchain, installed and in order

features.16: omega docker shows what images, volumes and build cache take, and cleans only what you tick. Docker cleanups always ask first.
features.18: omega full walks through all of it in one interface: a plan that says what each stage does and why, the route always in view, and skip, repeat or stop between stages. omega menu lists every command to pick from.
features.20: Type omega why is my disk full, or "undo yesterday's Dock change" inside a session. What the command line does, the agent can do too.
features.22: omega quick empties trash, removes safe caches, checks pending updates, and reports battery and disk health in seconds with zero risk.
features.24: Audit git repos with omega git, clean stale build artifacts with omega disk, flush DNS with omega net, and audit SSH and secrets with omega audit.
features.26: Run 100% offline with omega --no-ai, automate via background daemons with omega schedule, and output structured JSON with --json for CI/CD.

faq.q1: Does omega replace topgrade and Mole?
faq.a1: For a typical developer machine, yes. omega has its own steps for Homebrew, the Mac App Store and macOS on a Mac, for apt, dnf, pacman, zypper, Flatpak and snap on Linux, and on both for npm, pnpm, bun, pipx, uv, rustup, cargo, gh extensions, Oh My Zsh, caches, Docker and the Trash. If topgrade or Mole are installed, it also uses them and can fix their configuration with omega fix.
faq.q2: What does omega send to the AI provider?
faq.a2: Its instructions, the trimmed output of the commands it runs and the configuration files it reads. It is instructed never to open your documents. Every run is logged to ~/.local/state/omega/runs. omega logs lists those transcripts and omega logs view prints one. omega keeps the newest 30.
faq.q3: A command from this page says it does not exist. Why?
faq.a3: Your omega is older than this page, which describes the latest release: omega dev and omega menu, for example, arrived in 0.14.0. Run brew update && brew upgrade omega, then omega --version. omega doctor tells you when a newer release exists.
faq.a4: Whether a newer release exists, the config file, whether the API key looks like a key, whether the provider answers, and which maintenance steps are installed. It also reports the two models automatic mode will use. It lists models or probes a local server and never sends a chat message, so it does not spend tokens.
faq.a5: Only after you approve it. Deleting, sudo, editing config files and any unknown command need your confirmation. Commands like rm -rf ~ or rm -rf / (extra flags still count), diskutil erase or curl piped into a shell are blocked and never run, even with --yes.
faq.q6: Which AI models work with omega?
faq.a6: Any model with tool calling from Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter or OpenCode Zen, or a local one through Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI compatible endpoint. By default omega uses a fast model and switches to a stronger one when a step fails. Choose with omega model.
faq.q7: How does omega choose the model?
faq.a7: From live data, not from a list built into the program. Once a day it reads OpenRouter's public model catalogue, which carries list prices and the Artificial Analysis index, keeps the models your key can use and picks two: the fast one by score per dollar among models with at least 40% of the best score, and the smart one among models within 20% of the best. omega models shows the table and the picks. The request carries nothing about you, and omega config set model_catalog off stops it. The score is a general benchmark, not a test of maintenance work.
faq.q8: Can I change the mode or the model during a run?
faq.a8: Yes. shift tab cycles between asking before risky actions, auto approve and read only, and ctrl p switches to the next model of the run. Press ? for the shortcut card. In the input box, type / for commands such as /mode, /model and /exit: a menu explains each one as you type. A model you pick by hand is kept for the rest of the run. The first esc clears a line you have started; the next one ends the session. ctrl f searches the transcript: Enter jumps to the next match and Ctrl+P to the previous while search is open. ctrl y copies the focused tool output. Click a card row to select it, and click the key line to confirm.
faq.q9: How much does a run cost?
faq.a9: On the automatic model a typical run costs under one cent: a full configuration review on a real Mac came to $0.009. omega shows tokens and cost live in the status bar and in the final summary. Local models cost nothing.
faq.q10: Can it run on a local model?
faq.a10: Yes. Start Ollama or the LM Studio server and pick the provider in omega setup. Apple Intelligence's on device model is only reachable from Swift and its 4,096 token context is too small for this kind of agent, so omega uses local servers instead.
faq.q11: How does omega tune know the right settings?
faq.a11: It does not ship a fixed list. For each tool you have installed it gets pointers to the config files and the official docs, reads the current documentation on the web, and proposes changes with their source. You pick which ones to apply, or use --auto for the low risk ones.
faq.a12: Yes. Run omega update --yes --no-tui --once from launchd or cron. Blocked commands stay blocked, Docker is never cleaned without you, and recommendations go into the summary instead of a card.
faq.q13: What happens when something needs admin access?
faq.a13: Commands run detached from your terminal, so nothing can write over the interface. When a tool such as Mole or softwareupdate asks for sudo, omega shows a password card, checks the password with sudo and keeps it in memory for that run only. It is never logged or sent to the AI. Press Esc to skip the steps that need it.
faq.a14: Yes. On Linux omega checks, updates and cleans through apt, dnf, pacman, zypper, Flatpak, snap and Homebrew, reviews the systemd journal, keeps API keys in the system keyring or in a file only you can read, and installs developer tools with your distribution's packages. omega mac (login items, menu bar, Dock, shortcuts, privacy permissions, apps) and the Mac only steps do not exist on Linux.
faq.a15: Yes, on Windows 10 and 11. omega runs its commands in PowerShell, checks and updates through winget, Scoop and Chocolatey, lists pending Windows updates, reviews the event log, cleans temporary files, the Recycle Bin and the component store, and keeps API keys in the Windows Credential Manager. It never elevates itself: steps that need administrator rights work when the terminal was opened as administrator. omega mac is Mac only, and installing Windows updates is left to Windows Update.
faq.q16: Can omega sort out login items, the menu bar and shortcut conflicts?
faq.a16: Yes, with omega mac. It lists what opens at login, what is allowed in the background, menu bar apps, the Dock and global keyboard shortcuts, and suggests changes from your rules (~/.config/omega/mac.toml) and its defaults: updaters off, chat and AI assistants opened when needed, VPN, security and sync kept, and AI assistants that grab a shortcut on install moved to a free one. Your choices are saved for next time, and omega mac undo reverts any change.
faq.q17: Can omega clean the list of privacy permissions?
faq.a17: Yes, with omega mac permissions. It finds the entries in System Settings → Privacy & Security whose binary no longer exists (an app that bundles node in a versioned folder leaves one per update) or whose app is gone, names each with its version, and removes the ones you pick after saving a copy of the database. Reading your own list needs Full Disk Access for the terminal. Entries macOS protects system-wide, such as Full Disk Access, Accessibility and Screen Recording, are found but have to be removed by you in System Settings.
faq.q18: Can omega install and set up my developer tools?
faq.a18: Yes, with omega dev. It knows more than 70 languages, version managers and command-line tools. omega dev status shows what is installed and by which manager, and points out overlapping version managers, commands that resolve to the wrong copy and PATH entries that do not exist. omega dev install installs what you pick and omega dev activate adds the shell line a tool needs to ~/.zshrc, keeping a copy of the file.
faq.q19: Is there one command that does everything?
faq.a19: Yes: omega full. It opens on a plan with every stage that applies to your machine (the setup check, a read-only report, health and security, updates, cleanup, Docker, tool configuration, the developer setup, on a Mac what runs outside your apps, the repair of topgrade and Mole, and what earlier runs left undone), each with what it does and why, and you untick the ones you do not want. The stages then run one after another in the same interface, with the route always in view; between two stages you can go on, skip the next, repeat one that failed, change the plan or stop, and at the end it lists what was done, skipped and failed. omega health runs the health and security review on its own, and omega alone is the quick version: check, update, clean and summarise in one session.
faq.q20: Can I just tell it what I want?
faq.a20: Yes. In a session, type what you need: "install fzf and mise", "undo yesterday's Dock change", "what failed last time?", "which model should I use?". The agent can install tools, revert Mac changes, read earlier runs, manage its notes, change settings and run the setup check, asking before each change. It cannot read your API keys, change the provider or change the approval policy: for those it gives you the command.
faq.a21: Yes. The same agent runs in a window on macOS, Linux and Windows, with the same tasks, safety policy, configuration and keys as the command. On a Mac, brew install --cask lcajigasm/tap/omega-app installs it, or download the disk image from the release; Windows and Linux have the omega-gui archives. The builds are not signed yet, so macOS and Windows ask before the first run.
faq.a22: On a Mac, or on Linux with Homebrew, brew install lcajigasm/tap/omega for the command and brew install --cask lcajigasm/tap/omega-app for the desktop app on a Mac. GitHub Releases also attach archives of both for macOS, Linux and Windows, amd64 and arm64, with checksums.
faq.q23: Where are my API keys stored?
faq.a23: In the macOS Keychain, under the service omega-cli. On Windows, in the Credential Manager. On Linux, in the system keyring (Secret Service) when one answers, otherwise in ~/.config/omega/keys, a file only you can read; omega says which one it used. Environment variables such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY take precedence when set.
faq.q24: Which languages does the interface support?
faq.a24: English, Spanish, French, German and Portuguese, in the command, in the desktop app and on this website. omega follows your system locale, and you can override it with omega config set language. The agent replies in the same language.

privacy.11: omega doctor asks GitHub (api.github.com) for the tag of the latest omega release, to tell you when yours is older. The request carries nothing about you; GitHub may log your IP address. No other command makes it.
privacy.13: This site is hosted on GitHub Pages and loads fonts from Google Fonts, icons from unpkg and, on the home page, the session player from jsDelivr. Those services may log your IP address as part of serving the files.
privacy.15: Questions or concerns: open an issue at github.com/lcajigasm/omega/issues.
privacy.3: omega is a command line tool and a desktop app. Both run on your machine. It has no account, no server of its own, no analytics and no telemetry. This website sets no cookies; when you pick a language, it remembers the choice in your browser.
privacy.5: Your API keys are stored in the macOS Keychain under the service omega-cli. On Windows they are stored in the Credential Manager. On Linux they are stored in the system keyring (Secret Service) or, when there is none, in ~/.config/omega/keys, a file only your user can read. Your configuration lives in ~/.config/omega/config.toml, the notes the agent keeps about your machine in ~/.config/omega/notes.md, and a log of every run in ~/.local/state/omega/runs. You can delete any of them at any time.
privacy.6: What goes to your AI provider
privacy.7: omega talks only to the provider you configure: Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter or OpenCode Zen. Each request contains omega's instructions, your notes, the trimmed output of the commands it ran and the contents of the configuration files it read. The agent is instructed not to read personal documents. That provider's own privacy policy and data retention terms apply to those requests.
privacy.9: To choose the models of automatic mode, omega downloads OpenRouter's public model list from openrouter.ai once a day, also when your provider is another one. It is a plain request with no key and nothing about you or your machine in it; OpenRouter may log your IP address as part of serving it. omega config set model_catalog off stops it, and local providers never make it.
